title: Check yourself: `tool_choice`, the call that must happen, caps on irreversible tools, and the practice

questions.stem: To force a first tool on a model that rejects forcing, a team offers only that tool in the first request and the full list in every later one. Which cost does the first change carry?

options.text: Only the message blocks are processed again, as for any change of tool choice
options.says: Ruled out because that holds only for the choice: "Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache".

options.text: Nothing is processed again, since definitions that are removed stay cached
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason, since the list is part of the cached prefix: "Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache".

options.text: Only the system prompt is processed again, because it sits above the messages
options.says: Ruled out because the layers cascade downward: "Changes at each level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels."

options.text: The whole cached prefix is processed again, since the definitions differ
options.says: Changing the definitions changes the first layer of the cache, and every layer after it.

origin.section: `tool_choice`, the call that must happen, caps on irreversible tools, and the practice

questions.stem: A loop on a model that rejects forced tool use offers one tool with automatic choice, and a reply comes back as plain text with no tool call. What should the loop do?

options.text: Accept the text as the answer and go on to the next step
options.says: Ruled out because "A reply of text only, when a call was required, is a miss".

options.text: Resend the request with `any` as the choice and expect a call
options.says: Ruled out because the parameter is refused there: "`any` and `tool` return a 400 error".

options.text: Count it as a miss and ask once more before escalating
options.says: With `auto` the table's guarantee is "Nothing: it may answer in text", so a missed call is a miss that the loop handles.

options.text: Repeat the same request until the turn limit ends the run
options.says: Ruled out because "Looping until the turn limit turns a missed call into a run that ends with nothing".
